narration.oldText: Swap partners: copper hydroxide and sodium sulfate. Sodium sulfate is soluble. Hydroxides are insoluble unless they're with Group 1, so copper(II) hydroxide precipitates, a pale blue solid. Copper is two plus, so it needs two hydroxides: copper ion plus two hydroxide ions gives copper hydroxide solid. If you wrote C u O H, the charges don't balance.
